<Subject 2> — 钱经理 (S3): a 45-year-old male property manager. Slightly overweight, slicked-back oily hair, round face, an ingratiating smile that flips into a scowl, white shirt with a dark grey waistcoat, dark trousers and a staff badge. His voice is loud, nasal and bullying, standard Mandarin. It is the person shown in <Picture 2>.
<Subject 3> — 苏小满 (S1): a 25-year-old female cleaner. Preserve her exact face, small lean build, centre-parted black hair in a low practical ponytail, plain dark-navy housekeeping shirt with rolled sleeves, a worn grey-blue apron over navy trousers, black cloth shoes and a small keyring at her waist. Her voice is low, steady and slightly hoarse, standard Mandarin. It is the person shown in <Picture 3>.
<Picture 4>: the 3rd-floor ballroom corridor of 景宸大厦 — beige mirror-polished marble, floor-to-ceiling windows along the left, deep-red double doors with gold ornament and a lit chandelier beyond, a gold cleaning cart by the right wall. Use as the exact location and lighting reference; the people in it are not copied.

detailed_description:
VERTICAL 9:16 PORTRAIT FRAME — the picture is much taller than it is wide, composed for a phone screen: stage the action in DEPTH, front-to-back, and never spread people out left-to-right; keep faces and bodies in the upper two thirds of the frame, and let one strong foreground element run along the bottom edge (desk corner, tiled floor, doorframe, car seat) to give depth. Two people talk in an over-the-shoulder or one-behind-the-other arrangement, never side by side. STAGE DIRECTION — THIS IS A NARRATIVE SCENE, NOT A CLOSE-UP: the subject is a whole adult figure standing at working height, framed from at least the knees up, and the camera holds that same framing for the entire take. A standing person stays STANDING — the torso is upright, leaning forward at most about fifteen degrees, while the hands do the work at waist or chest level. The head stays level and the face turns toward the task or toward the other person, eyes open and readable. One clear action per beat, held steady: the framing stays the same width throughout, and the camera neither pushes in nor tilts down onto her hands, and the shot never tightens to a detail view of an object while someone is speaking. LIGHTING IS SOFT, BRIGHT AND FLATTERING — this instruction overrides any instinct to light the scene moodily. Use one very large wrapping soft source (a big diffused window or a 4x4 softbox) placed close to the subject, with soft fill coming in from the front, so every face is evenly lit, fully open and easy to read. Keep SHADOW DENSITY LOW: shadows stay pale, open, gentle and full of detail — never black, never deep, never heavy, never hard-edged. There is no hard shadow on any face: no dark band under the eyes, no black shadow under the nose or the chin, no harsh nose or jaw shadow, no strong contrast across the cheek. Hair and dark clothing must still show visible texture and sheen instead of crushing to a black mass. Expose one stop brighter than a natural reading, with lifted blacks and open milky midtones, like a bright soft-lit beauty commercial. The result must feel tender, airy and luminous — soft light everywhere, no gloom, no muddy darker corners. Premium modern urban short drama, shot on a large-format cinema camera with warm anamorphic character, shallow depth of field and soft oval bokeh, fine 35mm film grain, a warm low-contrast film grade with lifted blacks, open midtones and soft highlight roll-off. The image must read BRIGHT, luminous, soft, clean and expensive — glowing diffused window light wrapped in soft front fill, spotless surfaces, elegant production design. Absolutely NOT dark, not contrasty, not murky, not moody. Beautiful photogenic cast with refined features and flawless skin, elegant wardrobe and hair. Camera work stays high-end cinematic: slow controlled dolly moves, gentle handheld, precise rack focus, natural 24fps motion blur.
STAGE DIRECTION — THIS IS A NARRATIVE SCENE, NOT A CLOSE-UP: the subject is a whole adult figure standing at working height, framed from at least the knees up, and the camera holds that same framing for the entire take. A standing person stays STANDING — the torso is upright, leaning forward at most about fifteen degrees, while the hands do the work at waist or chest level. The head stays level and the face turns toward the task or toward the other person, eyes open and readable. One clear action per beat, held steady: the framing stays the same width throughout, and the camera neither pushes in nor tilts down onto her hands, and the shot never tightens to a detail view of an object while someone is speaking. 
ABSOLUTELY NO SUBTITLES, NO CAPTIONS, NO LOWER-THIRDS, NO TITLE CARDS, NO WATERMARKS AND NO BURNED-IN TEXT of any kind anywhere in the frame — the delivered clip must be clean picture with no typography over it, so that subtitles can be added later in post. Any spoken line is AUDIO ONLY and must never appear written on screen. The only text that may exist is lettering physically printed on a real object inside the scene (for example the gilt character stamped into the face of the black card, or signage already present in the location). 
BACKGROUND PEOPLE: every background person must be a DISTINCT individual — a different face shape, different hair, different clothing colour, different height and age from every other person in frame. NEVER let a background person share, copy, echo or approximate the face of a named subject: if 苏小满 (S1) is in shot, no other woman in the frame may have her face. Keep background faces turned away, in profile, lowered, or softly out of focus so no second face reads as clearly as the subject's; at most two background faces may be recognisable at once, and never two identical-looking ones. Do not add people beyond the ones this beat names, and never duplicate a person to fill the frame. 
Speaker labels are stable for the whole series: (S1) 苏小满, (S2) 女贵宾, (S3) 钱经理, (S4) 小唐, (S5) 阿芳, (S6) 周总监, (S7) 小罗, (S8) 陆蔓, (S9) 外婆, (S10) 张总, (S11) 医生, (S12) 前台, (S13) 陆家接线人（只在电话里，从不出现）, (S14) 陆航（只在门内画外，从不出现）. Anyone not given a numbered line stays completely silent with a closed mouth.
Fixed spatial set-up for the whole corridor scene, never change it: the gold cleaning cart is parked against the RIGHT-hand wall with its head pointing away down the corridor towards the far red doors, and the cart itself never moves. 苏小满 (S1) is always on the LEFT side of that cart — the corridor side — with the cart to her RIGHT, half a step behind the handle, both hands on the handle unless she is kneeling to wipe. When she kneels she kneels a half-step in front-left of the cart, the cart still to her RIGHT against the RIGHT wall; the cart never moves. 女贵宾 (S2) always stands in the middle-left of the corridor about two metres away, facing her. Daylight floods in from the floor-to-ceiling windows on the LEFT. 苏小满 and the cart always stay in the RIGHT half of frame; the guest always stays in the LEFT half of frame. Never mirror, swap or re-arrange this. Her grey cleaning cloth is always in her RIGHT hand until she is made to switch it.
Exposure, white balance and colour must match the reference images exactly — bright, clean, warm daylight, luminous skin, open shadows. Re-light this segment from scratch as soft, bright beauty lighting: one big wrapping soft source plus visible front fill, faces evenly lit with LOW shadow density, no hard or heavy shadow on any skin, no black shadow under the eyes, nose or chin, lifted blacks and open midtones. It must look tender and luminous, never hard, never moody. Do NOT inherit the tone, grain, contrast or darkness of any previous clip; continuity is in the character positions and props only, never in the lighting. Never return a clip darker or more contrasty than the reference images.
Entry state, re-anchored to the reference images: 钱经理 (S3) is bent low at the guest's rear-right shoulder; the guest (S2) stands in the middle-left of the corridor; 苏小满 (S1) is on the left side of her cart, which is still against the RIGHT wall, in the right of frame.
[Shot 1] Medium shot, slightly low: 女贵宾 (S2) stands with her chin up and her shoulders squared in the left half of frame, then lifts her right hand and points a manicured finger straight past the manager's shoulder, down the corridor to the right of frame, towards the cleaner.
[Shot 2] At 00:02.400, close on 女贵宾's (S2) face as she spits the accusation in clipped ringing Mandarin, one staccato phrase at a time, her fingertip trembling with anger: [Chinese] 她！她的车蹭的！这条裙子两万八！她赔得起吗！
[Shot 3] At 00:06.800, reverse over her shoulder: 苏小满 (S1) is small in the right of frame on the left side of her cart; 钱经理 (S3) is beside her in frame with his smile frozen. Neither of them speaks.
[Shot 4] At 00:08.600, quick tilt up and along the corridor to the onlookers, guests and staff all turning to stare.
